newsitem.title: UK: Dry cargo freight market heading higher.
newsitem.headline: Dry cargo freight market heading higher.

text.p: Despite a modest rise in the Baltic Freight Index today of 5 points to 1445 market conditions have continued to move steadily in favour of owners in the majority of the dry cargo trades.

Brokers said Panamax rates were still climbing in the Atlantic and were at the very least stable in the east, with certain areas such as S.E.Asia showing greater strength. The recent healthier demand for Capers seen in the Pacific now appears to be reaching the Atlantic. Handies were especially firm from Argentina/Brazil, and charterers indicated higher levels for craned tonnage from the continent to the far east.

GRAIN - Significantly higher rates were reported and rumoured in the Atlantic Panamax grain trades. Cargill booked Patmos for about 62,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Antwerp-Hamburg range (with other options) for Dec 10/19 at lumpsum equivalent of $13.10, and may have a possible enquiry for repeat business.

Hanjin fixed the continental-relet Scenery Sea for 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for mid Dec at between $24.00 and $24.50 no combo, a jump of $1.00/1.50 from First Steamship's fixture of Ever Blessing in this trade 10 days ago.

Timecharter levels also showed impressive firmness. Joyous Age 69,271 dwt open Baltimore mid Dec was reported fixed for a trip to the far east at about $14,500 daily plus $250,000 bonus and there was also speculation Cho Yang had fixed Paiute 70,293 dwt delivery Quebec about Dec 10 for a trip to the far east at close to $15,000 daily. A December Panamax was rumored booked for US Gulf/China grain, and Peljesac 71,229 dwt may have gone to Sinochart in the same trade.
Other vessels said chartered for US Gulf/far east included Narwal 67,000 dwt prompt Montoir, Bright State 68,000 dwt Ghent Dec 11, and Global Epica 62,000 dwt open Morocco Dec 16.
Continental Spirit 65,224 dwt was rumoured fixed delivery US Gulf for 2 laden legs, and Bechet 65,418 dwt open prompt Constanza was reported covered on private terms.

In the east Toscana 63,159 dwt was fixed for Australian grain to Bin Qasim, possibly by Shadab, but failed on subjects, and Petriana 64,911 dwt was believed fixed from Indonesia by Pan Ocean for similar business at a very firm rate in the region of $12,000/12,500 daily, but also failed on subjects.
Dreyfus were rumoured to have fixed a Panamax for US Gulf/Japan, but details were not avlable.
Most of the handy-size grain activity was in the Plate and Brazil where rates were said to be appreciating rapidly, but information was being kept private by charterers as far as possible.
Continental fixed Seram 25,592 dwt delivery Durban trip via Argentina redlivery Tunisia at $7,000 daily but failed on subjects, and are said to have taken Paris Junior instead on private terms.
Nan Fung 34,999 dwt was fixed by unnamed charterers delivery W.Africa for Plate grain business.
In the north Atlantic reports from New York indicated that Saroc fixed World Agamemnon 37,678 dwt delivery US East Coast trip Brazil in the low $7,000's daily.
Not a great deal of fresh grain business was quoted today but brokers believed that there was enough in the market already at least to sustain current levels for December.

MINERALS - Conditions for Capers were lively in most areas. The 20-year old Lika 118,733 dwt was booked by Deiulemar for two non-grain transatlantic rounds at a firmer $10,500 daily, and single rounds were understood fixed by Exemplar 123,000 dwt and Ostracho 125,000 dwt, possibly at around $12,000/13,000 daily.

Brasilux fixed Tubarao/Rotterdam ironore contracts for Feb 1997-Jan 1998 - rumoured 1 million tonnes in 140,000 tonne lots with Yukong Capers in the region of $6.00. In the east Iron Yandi 169,000 dwt was believed fixed for NSW/Japan business on private terms.

HANDY-SIZES - A number of vessels have been fixed from the continent - Nikolaos P 34,750 dwt, for example, to Western Bulkcarriers from Stettin to US Gulf, Balaji Premium 36,205 dwt also from Stettin for Atlantic business, and a Hanjin 28,000 dwt craned bulker from Skaw to the US Gulf to Brodin at $7,350 daily.

Older vessels such as Unison 44,000 dwt went to Poseidon Continent/Arabian Gulf at $10,500 daily plus $45,000 bonus, and Ferropos were linked with an over-age 28,000 dwt vessel lower Baltic/US gulf at about $5,500 daily.
